entries.title: I Corinthians 4:5
segments: His praise from God. Such praise as belongs to him in God's perfect judgment.

entries.title: I Corinthians 4:6
segments: The things which are written. No special text, but the teaching of the Scriptures as a whole, which no leader, however gifted, may supersede.

entries.title: I Corinthians 4:7
segments: Who maketh thee to differ? 'Thee' is general in meaning, equivalent to 'any one,' especially any one of the opposing teachers.  The English 'you' is often so used: 'you will find,' that is, any one will find.  In this and the following verses, Paul addresses the opposing teachers, first in the singular, then in the plural number, as if addressing them personally.  'Any superiority which any of you has is but the gift of God, not a cause of pride or partisanship.'
